authority: Bounded read-only native subscription authentication/isolation investigation. Dean rejects API-key path. No key or environment binding requested; no live/login/implementation authority inferred.

conclusion.isolatedNativeClientWithFreshOfficialLog: Feasible in principle for native-only use; not executed or fully qualified here.
conclusion.reuseExistingLoginWithGuaranteedZeroShar: NO supported zero-write guarantee found. Shared credential refresh/save/lock paths remain part of the native auth lifecycle.
conclusion.newAdapterOrBridgeFeasibility: UNKNOWN until a separately scoped integration contract and offline prototype preserve Subswitch HTTP/model/tool semantics. Not a configuration switch.
conclusion.release061Dependency: Independent. The reviewed0.6.1 release is the prior future-model alias/doctor fix and excludes routing PR81/85/87/88. Kimi native auth work neither becomes supported by that release nor must block its separate release process.
conclusion.recommendedNextAction: Keep the key-based runner preserved and inactive. Route a separate Kimi subscription-native destination design/implementation task before further through-Subswitch validation. Evaluate official opaque-auth CLI/ACP integration against caller-owned tool semantics; if it cannot satisfy the model-destination contract, establish a supported managed-provider SDK integration contract. Qualify offline before any bounded login/live phase.

gateCorrection.interpretation: The passed native login/text/tool gate remains passed. It never demonstrated Subswitch destination OAuth, Messages/Responses compatibility or fallback. Current login status was not re-read; Dean reports the machine is authorized.

actualAdapter.finding: supportsNativeOAuth accepts only codex/chatgpt-codex and claude/claude-code; Kimi products are absent.

Configuration requires the native-oauth credential kind exactly when supportsNativeOAuth is true. Kimi native-oauth is rejected with credential_product_mismatch; env credential is the implemented Kimi path.

Native manager construction/get/refresh guard against unsupported Kimi OAuth before saved-auth access. Kimi env profile creates Bearer headers from its explicitly supplied environment credential. There is no Kimi CLI/ACP/SDK transport or token lifecycle here.
Kimi destination catalog exposes Messages/Responses HTTP protocols. Official native CLI/ACP is an agent/session interface, not this raw model destination protocol.

The preserved runner deliberately targets that existing adapter, constructs credential.kind=env, and requires a coding-plan-key authorization binding. It cannot use native login without changing source/authorization/runtime assumptions. Dean has now rejected its key-based live path.

findings.fact: Kimi Code managed authentication is OAuth. The official CLI login/device-code flow stores and automatically refreshes native credentials; no API key is needed for the native client.
KIMI_CODE_HOME relocates native configuration, credential files, sessions and logs. Instances sharing it share config/credentials. Generic .agents resources have a separate OS-home discovery root.
Official ACP uses a dedicated JSON-RPC stdin/stdout subprocess with session/prompt/tool/permission operations and native authentication. It is not a drop-in Messages or Responses model endpoint.

The repository exports KimiForCodingProvider with homeDir/model/baseUrl and an opaque managed OAuth toolkit. Its native provider is type=kimi; it can refresh on401 and retry the request once. This is a useful official implementation reference, not evidence that the current Subswitch adapter already supports it.

At this pinned head, node-sdk0.21.0 and OAuth toolkit0.4.0 are marked private:true. Their short READMEs refer to the monorepo; no reviewed standalone consumer compatibility promise was established. Do not infer public package availability or a stable supported plug-in from source exports alone. No registry install/probe was performed.

Native ensureFresh can take a cross-process lock and persist refreshed tokens; token storage writes atomically. Reusing the current credential directory is intentionally shared behavior, not read-only isolation.

installedClient.discovery: PATH executable metadata and known distribution files only; never executed the CLI or loaded user config/auth/history.
installedClient.qualification: Public current source and installed bundled version differ in SDK version. Installed runtime is separately inventoried; no upgrade or equality to current main is claimed.

isolationAssessment.status: Unresolved for using the existing login without shared writes
isolationAssessment.finding: An empty isolated home has no existing native login. Pointing credential storage at the original home can refresh/save/lock credentials there. No secret-free documented operation was found to attach the existing login to an independent writable home without copying/repurposing credentials.
isolationAssessment.safeDirection: Future explicitly authorized official login in a new private home, with credentials kept opaque inside the native toolchain. No copying/extracting/printing existing tokens.

isolationAssessment.status: Can isolate local state with prerequisites
isolationAssessment.finding: Use a new cwd/session and fresh HOME, XDG roots, KIMI_CODE_HOME and TMPDIR, not continue/load/resume or shared native home. Verify OS-home discovery is also redirected or disabled; KIMI_CODE_HOME alone is insufficient.
isolationAssessment.uncertainty: Fresh OAuth grant server-side multi-device behavior was not established. Local filesystem separation does not promise account/quota separation.

isolationAssessment.finding: Prefer a dedicated stdio ACP process if a bridge is chosen; no shared server is required by that interface. Any loopback relay gets its own captured OS-assigned port and owned capability, no shared-proxy discovery.
isolationAssessment.avoid: No existing server shutdown/restart, server kill, token rotation, logout, session listing/resume/delete or browser remote-control attachment.

isolationAssessment.finding: Official web mode registers per-home instances and uses a per-home server token. Rotation affects all instances sharing that home. It adds REST/WebSocket/session lifecycle rather than raw model API semantics.

Drop inherited HTTP(S)/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY variants, provider keys/other-client routing variables, Node preloads and Kimi endpoint/model overrides. Set only reviewed fixed native settings. Disable auto-update, telemetry and cron; keep hooks/MCP/plugins/skills absent or explicitly owned. Pin executable, Node, complete distribution/dependencies/config before launch.

Installed main runs update preflight even in prompt mode and installs/cleans native workers/caches during bootstrap. A future process needs its own temp/cache roots and documented KIMI_CODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1. No version/help invocation was needed or performed here.

Subswitch currently returns tool calls for the originating Claude/Codex client to execute. Native Kimi is a full agent and can execute its own tools; ACP exposes reverse RPC, permissions and terminal/filesystem capabilities. A bridge must preserve tool ownership, exact call IDs/results, streaming errors, cancellation and affinity without an extra autonomous agent loop or duplicate tool execution.
Inference under the same subscription would consume its entitlement. Filesystem/process isolation cannot promise separate quota. No usage/metadata/entitlement request was made.

newNativeCapFinding.fact: Documented KIMI_MODEL_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS, KIMI_LOOP_MAX_STEPS_PER_TURN and KIMI_LOOP_MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_STEP controls are present in the installed2.1.1 bundle. The cap overlay feeds maxCompletionTokens; the Kimi wire trait encodes max_completion_tokens.
newNativeCapFinding.usefulCorrection: Native per-step output limiting has a documented candidate; it is not simply missing because the CLI has no max-token flag. Prior native harness qualification remains pending, rather than being impossible for lack of any control.
newNativeCapFinding.notYetQualified: No offline native transport execution or live wire capture here. Per-step caps/attempt controls do not alone prove a global six-dispatch ceiling, no lower-level retries,30s full-body deadlines or all-request accounting. The managed provider can refresh/retry on401; auxiliary requests, compaction, subagents and projection retries require explicit controls. Do not substitute headers-timeout for total request deadline.

offlineFirst: Select a maintained documented native interface and write an adapter contract preserving originating HTTP protocol/history and caller tool ownership. Verify that it is a model destination rather than a nested agent with changed semantics.

Implement and independently review an isolated no-key adapter/harness in a separate task. Use fabricated OAuth/storage and owned loopback transport to test missing auth, refresh/account ownership, request caps, retries/counts, errors, tool handoff, cancellation and cleanup.

Fingerprint the exact native runtime/distribution/dependencies and config. Prove positive environment, isolated OS/Kimi homes, no shared daemon/port/native store discovery, ancillary-network refusal and complete process/state cleanup.
minimalFuturePlan.authenticationPrerequisite: Only after a separately authorized bounded authentication setup: official subscription login in the owned Kimi home, handled by its native toolchain with no token extraction. Device-code polling/auth endpoints need their own finite reviewed allowlist/deadline; the prior inference-only runner does not authorize them.
minimalFuturePlan.livePrerequisite: Coordinator confirms product/region/model, isolated OAuth setup, protocol/continuity gates and amended executable plan after implementation review. Do not run the old key-bound runner or relabel a standalone native-client test as through-Subswitch validation.
minimalFuturePlan.authority: Proposal only, not execution approval. A new CLI bridge/protocol or OAuth setup is not automatically covered by the existing key-based phaseA implementation.

releaseIndependence.conclusion: Keep the0.6.1 release process separate. Native Kimi auth remains new work and is not a release dependency for that reviewed scope. Current publish/signoff/registry status belongs to coordinator; this investigation did not inspect npm credentials or query registry.

boundaries.networkScope: Only public official GitHub API/raw source and web documentation reads.

nextAction: Stop this read-only investigation. Coordinator explains missing native-subscription destination implementation, supersedes the key-name wait, keeps0.6.1 independent, and scopes the no-key adapter contract/offline work. No live or native-login action from this report.
